links.reason: Both call a shore bird as witness of the lover's conduct (தான்கண்டு, அருள்அற் றிடக்கண்டும்), a real shared figure. But nothing in Kainnilai 50 says she still hopes the oath will hold: she refuses to speak to him (நின்னோடு உரையேன்), so the 'stage of trust' contrast in teaches is imposed; the pairing is a shared image, not a qualification.

Pazhamozhi 14 says the good things said before the unlearned turn bad (நல்லவும் தீயவாம்), Nanmanikkadigai 97 that the learned man himself has no standing there (கற்றான் ஒருவனும் பாடிலனே). The note reports both accurately and the words/speaker distinction is a real, specific difference.

Maduraikkanchi names the victory at Alankanam as the patron's deed (ஆலங் கானத் தஞ்சுவர விறுத்து அரசு பட), and Akananuru 209 uses the same battle's roar (ஆலங் கானத்து ஆர்ப்பினும் பெரிது) as the measure of village gossip. A puram event serving as an akam measure is exactly the kind of named link the note describes.

Kural 1216's waking (நனவு) is ordinary waking from a dream; Kural 339's waking (விழிப்பது) is a figure for birth. The link rests only on the shared word, and the teaches sentence itself admits nothing in the verse supports the reading.

Akananuru 28 makes the loss of the guard depend on her failing to scare the parrots (சிறு கிளி கடிதல் தேற்றாள் இவள்), Ainkurunuru 289 on her voice drawing them (இன்குரல் கிளிசெத்து), and only the latter ends with வரைந்தனை கொண்மோ. The contrast between a mendable and an unmendable cause is in the Tamil.

Both reward the guest-calling crow (விருந்துவரக் கரைந்த காக்கை; வரக்கரைந் தீமே), Kuruntokai 210 after the return with seven bowls called too little, Ainkurunuru 391 before it with a promised gold bowl. Before/after the omen is a specific difference the pair shows.

Kalittokai 37 says outright that, since he cannot speak and for her to speak is unwomanly (பெண் அன்று, உரைத்தல் நமக்கு), she resolved on one shameless act (துணிதந்து, ஓர் நாண் இன்மை செய்தேன்). Against Kural 1257, where shame is lost when the lover acts, this is a real qualification.

Kural 1157 has the slipping bangles proclaim his desertion (துறைவன் துறந்தமை தூற்றா); Kuruntokai 117's friend turns the same sign into a jibe, smaller bangles are on sale (சிறியவும் உளவீண்டு விலைஞர்கை வளையே). The shift from lament to mockery is in the Tamil.

Kuruntokai 225 conditions the gift of her hair on his not forgetting a kindness (நன்றிமறந் தமையா யாயின்) like a king who forgets help once enthroned; Kural 110 ranks killing a benefit as beyond escape. The rule turned into a marriage condition is specific.

Both mothers of the eloped girl speak of the youth's mother (தாயே): in Akananuru 195 she will paint her walls in joy (பூவல் ஊட்டி ... உவந்து), in Ainkurunuru 373 she is wished the same weeping (நினைத்தொறும் கலிழும் இடும்பை எய்துக). 'Envy' slightly overreads 195, which sets her own nurture against the other's joy, but the counter-figure is real.

The rare shared term தற்சேர்ந்தார் / தற்சேர்ந் தவரை carries the same duty of supporting dependants, applied in Ainthinai Aimpathu 48 by the friend to the lover's renown (மிக்க மிகுபுகழ் தாங்குபவோ). A maxim applied to love is a genuine development.

The closing line உண்கண் சிவப்ப அழுதுநின் றோளே is shared, with river flood and sand-play (வண்டல்) in the marutham poem and the wave and doll (தெண்டிரை பாவை வெளவ) in the neythal one. The stock jibe adapted to the landscape is shown by the pair.

Both answer the rebukers (இடிக்குங் கேளிர்; நும்மினும் அறிகுவென்மன்னே) and do so differently, conceding their aim versus claiming to know better. But the teaches clause that 'sight of her has overridden' the rebuke comes only from Natrinai 160 (காணா ஊங்கே); Kuruntokai 58 speaks of a spreading sickness, not sight.

Kuruntokai 53's எம் அணங்கினவே says the oath torments us, which is the women's anxiety over a broken vow, not a doctrine that the god punishes them; Paripadal 8.66 (நின்னை ... மெய் வேல் தின்னும்) names the perjurer as struck. The two can both be true, so the tension depends on stretching அணங்கு.
links.text_issue: Paripadal 8 line 52 has a lacuna and the speaker turns in 51-55 are uncertain.

links.reason: Patitruppattu 89 gives the plenty as caused by நின்கோல் செம்மையின், the very claim of Kural 545 (இயல்புளிக் கோலோச்சும் மன்னவன் நாட்ட பெயலும் விளையுளும்). The connection is true but it is the shared belief; that the poem lists more things is thin, and the two agree rather than develop.

The phrase தீம்பால் பிலிற்ற is shared, but in Akananuru 14 the evening of the homing cows is the measure of his forgetting (மாலையும் உள்ளார் ஆயின்), not a cue that he is coming. The chariot the bard sees is not an answer to Thinaimozhi 30, so the 'fixed cue' claim overreaches.

The onlookers' formula யார்கொல் அளியர் தாமே is shared; Kuruntokai 7 leaves it as pity over the dangerous waste, Ainkurunuru 381 resolves it with the magandril pair (உடன்புணர் கொள்கைக் காதலோரே). That அளியர் spans pity and admiration is shown by the pair.

Kuruntokai 8's courtesan mocks the man as a mirror-puppet of his son's mother (ஆடிப் பாவை போல மேவன செய்யும்), which is scorn akin to Kural 906's (பாடிலரே), not a claim incompatible with it. 'The love poem's victory of the wife' is not in the poem, which voices only the rival's spite.

The shared word is பெயர்: names planted on hero-stones (செல்லா நல்லிசைப் பெயரொடு நட்ட) and men who died taking their names with them (தம்பெயர் தம்மொடு கொண்டனர் மாய்ந்தோர்). The giving/not-giving contrast turns on one reading of இலமென மலர்ந்த கையர் (552), which the Tamil does not fix.

Both are overheard speech about the mother's veri rite; Akananuru 242 states the remedy and its deadline (மறிஉயிர் வழங்கா அளவை ... முயங்கல் இயைவன்), Natrinai 47 only asks whether she may tell him (கூறின் எவனோ) and lets the bereaved elephant show the danger. The difference in directness is real.

Kuruntokai 165's toddy is a figure of one blow on top of another (மகிழ்ந்ததன் றலையும் நறவுண் டாங்கு), not a statement about liquor and sight. The poem never addresses Kural 1090's contrast (உண்டார்கண் அல்லது), so 'the comparison is turned around' is the linker's construction.

The shared term is அணங்கு, a question about what she is in Kural 1081 and the seizing power of her hair in Ainkurunuru 173 (கூந்தல் அணங்குற் றோரே). The Sangam poem does not answer the Kural's question; the teaches sentence dresses a shared word as a dialogue.

Puram 117 lists drought omens (மைம் மீன் புகையினும், தூமம் தோன்றினும்) and denies their effect under a straight sceptre (கோஒல் செம்மையின் ... பெயல் பிழைப்பு அறியா); Porunararruppadai grants the drought (பெருவறனாகிய பண்பில் காலையும்) and sets the Kaveri against it. Two strategies against a bad season are clearly distinguished.

Akananuru 46's buffalo breaks its tether at night and grazes the lotus (நோன் தளை பரிந்து ... தாமரை ... ஆரும்), Natrinai 260's has grazed the lilies, tired of the lotus (தாமரைப் பனிமலர் முணைஇ), and sleeps on the sand nearby. The same marutham creature fitted to different moments of the quarrel is a specific point.

Kar Narpathu 37's friend relies on the season and his king's task (வேந்தன் அருந்தொழில் வாய்த்த நமர்); Akananuru 304 shows the man held in the king's camp (வேந்தன் பாசறை வினையொடு வேறுபுலத்து அல்கி), dreading her reproach. The irony that the king's work is what keeps him is shown by the pair.

கூற்றின வல்வில் விடலை praises the youth's bow as deadly like Death, which is the usual sense of the epithet for a protector on the road; nothing in Thinaimozhi 20 makes the mother doubt him. The contrast with Natrinai 279 rests on reading praise as fear.

Song 12 credits the reconciliation to the river (வல்லதால், வையைப் புனல்), but song 7 ends with the sulk unresolved as the town bathes (செருவுற்றாள் செம் புனல் ஊருடன் ஆடுங்கடை). The claim that the hymns told the oodal 'in order to praise the flood as the reconciler' holds for one song, not the pair.
links.text_issue: Paripadal 12 line 59 is misnumbered in the source.

links.reason: Kural 218 says the discerning do not falter in ஒப்புரவு even in want (இடனில் பருவத்தும்); Innaa Narpathu 36 counts பொருளிலான் வேளாண்மை காமுறுதல் among painful things. That the same disposition is praised as duty and felt as pain is a real qualification.

Purananuru 35 spells out that the world blames the guardian when rain fails (மாரி பொய்ப்பினும் ... காவலர்ப் பழிக்கும்), Patitruppattu 89 credits the rain to the straight sceptre (நின்கோல் செம்மையின்). Credit and liability as two sides of one belief is specific and true.

Akananuru 387's lizard by the hero-stones turns back even lords with elephants (சிறிய தெற்றுவ தாயிற் ... நின்றாங்குப் பெயரும்); Kainnilai 18's truthful lizard (வாய்மாண்ட பல்லி) chirps as if it saw the return. The same omen read from road and home is a specific observation.

The distinctive simile of murukku buds as tiger's claws (உதிரம் துவரிய வேங்கை உகிர்போல்; வயமான் கோள்உகிர் அன்ன) is shared, and Ainthinai Aimpathu 31 itself says the season pleases those together (எதிருநர்க்கு இன்பம்). Akananuru 99 is that joy voiced by the man beside the girl.

Kural 1171 blames her own eyes (தாம்காட்ட யாம்கண் டது), Ainkurunuru 190 the lord with மன்ற (புலம்பன் மன்றஎம் ... பனிசெய் தோனே). The difference of direction is real, but the two claims are compatible, not a tension.

The man's oath in Kurinjippattu promises a house where the couple eat what is left after guests (விருந்துண் டெஞ்சிய மிச்சில் ... நின்னோ டுண்டலும் புரைவது), the purpose Kural 81 gives household life (விருந்தோம்பி வேளாண்மை செய்தற் பொருட்டு). The guest ethic as the content of a love oath is specific.

The hunter's question about the beast is shared (கெடுதியு முடையேன்; யாதோ, மற்று அம் மாதிறம் படர்). But Akananuru 48 already has the girls' silence (மெய்மறைபு ஒடுங்கி நாணி நின்றனெம்) and his reply to it (நும் வாய்ப் பொய்யும் உளவோ), so the idyll does not supply what the short poem lacks.

The son anchors the husband in both (பொலந்தொடிப் புதல்வனும் பொய்தல் கற்றனன்; பூங்கட் புதல்வனை நோக்கி). But Natrinai 166 puts her beauty first and the son 'on top' (அதன்தலை), and Akananuru 66 also credits his old kindness to her (பழங்கண் ணோட்டமும் நலிய), so 'rather than her own claim' is false.

The same poet uses Thazhumban's Unur in both (வாய்மொழித் தழும்பன் ஊணூர்; ஏஎர் தழும்பன் ஊணூர்), and chariots stand for suitors in both. But in Natrinai 300 the elephant is the begging lover, not the suitors' elephants, and the 'goad to the hidden lover' leans on the colophon's நொதுமலாளர் வரைவு more than the poem.

Pataliputra's gold is named in both (பொன்மலி பாடலி; நந்தர் சீர்மிகு பாடலி ... நிதியம்): Kuruntokai 75 offers it as reward for news of his coming, Akananuru 265 doubts that such wealth outweighs her. Opposite pricings of one measure are specific.

Both are kurinji monkey couples (மந்திக் கணவன் கல்லாக் கடுவன்; கைம்மை உய்யாக் காமர் மந்தி), and the two fears are a fair contrast. But neither poem draws the comparison; 'less faithful than the beast' and 'would not survive losing him' need a generous reading of the scenes.

Kural 584's ஒற்று is the king's spy who examines his own servants and kin; Thirikadugam 55's ஒற்றாள் are leaky intimates of any person. The verse does not explain the Kural's rule; the link turns on two senses of ஒற்று.

Ainkurunuru 431 has only peacocks on the rock (மணிநிற உருவின தோகையும் உடைத்தே), no konrai, so the note overstates. Reading its bare praise of the road as Kar Narpathu 4's 'medicine' (பசலை மருந்து) settles by fiat what the refrain leaves open.
links.text_issue: Kar Narpathu 4 line 4 is a repaired misprint.

links.reason: Both address the moon about being seen: Kural 1119 bids it not appear for many (பலர்காணத் தோன்றல்), Kuruntokai 47 says it is no good to night lovers (எல்லி வருநர் களவிற்கு நல்லை யல்லை). Compliment versus danger is a real difference of use.

The rare pair of words is shared: பகுத்துண்டு ... தொகுத்தவற்றுள் in Kural 322 and பகுத்(து)ஊண் தொகுத்த ஆண்மை in Patitruppattu 38. A virtue the Kural ranks under non-killing named as a king's manliness is a specific finding.

Both praise a Chera land by the 'no X but harmless Y' figure: Puram 20 (சோறு படுக்கும் தீயோடு செஞ் ஞாயிற்றுத் தெறல் அல்லது), Patitruppattu 28 (செந்நீர்ப் பூசல் அல்லது வெம்மை அரிது), which adds the drought. A convention bent to a new claim is shown.

Both set the buffalo in jackfruit shade in Kuttuvan's western land (பலவி னீழல் ... குடபுலங் காவலர்; தாமரை முனையின் முடமுதிர் பலவின் கொழுநிழல் வதியும் குடநாடு), and both outweigh it: Vanji is வறிதே beside the patron, Kudanadu would not keep the man from her. The idyll's buffalo grazed lilies (கழுநீர்), not the lotus, a small slip in the note.

poems.note: Line 4 is lost to a lacuna, so the poem's stated sense cannot be checked.
The crab-dragonfly-heron scene describes Maranthai inside an open simile for her beauty, and no two parts map onto the wedding situation.

ullurai.anchor: காலை வந்து மாலைப் பொழுதில் நல்லக நயந்துதான் உயங்கி

poems.note: The wind scattering the dune could figure the gossip of அலர்க இவ் ஊரே, but only that one match can be named.

iraicchi.act: the cock dove joins its hen at the evening hour
iraicchi.sense: the household doves pair at dusk while she cannot bear to be left alone, so he should not leave her

poems.note: கூர் எயிற்று எகினம் may be a dog rather than a swan; either way it only shivers.
Lines 1 to 3 are lost; nothing can be tagged.

iraicchi.act: the fierce tusker plays together with its mate in the cool season
iraicchi.sense: even the wild elephant is with its mate in this season, so the man's failure to come is the fault
